design: What the person sees and does, step by step. (1) Before: the plan card says under such a task 'More than a session's work budget (CHF 4.00): it pauses with its work kept and asks you to continue.'; the Start dialog keeps Start on and says in its amber note '"Build the shop" needs about CHF 6.00, more than this session's work budget of CHF 4.00: after the other tasks it works with about CHF 2.80, keeps its work, and asks you to continue.' (alone: '... it works until that budget is used, keeps its work, and asks you to continue.'); chat's 'start a session' reads the same warning back before its Yes. (2) The session runs everything that fits first, exactly as today, then the larger task with what is left of the work budget; one such task a session, and only when at least a fifth of the work budget is left, else it waits for the next session and the dialog said so. (3) Its runs are capped as every run is (its own budget left, else its specialist's limit per run; at most the session's work budget left; the project's budget, the month cap and the subscription's share through the hooks): nothing passes a limit, and the review reserve is never used for work. When it pauses at its specialist's limit per run, got further, and a fifth of the work budget is still left, the session runs it again at once from its kept work ('The coder goes on with "Build the shop" from where it stopped.'), with no card in between. (4) Before the step that could take a run past its line, the specialist hears what a good wrap-up is: finish the step you are on, start nothing new, leave what you changed building and running, undo or keep out of use a change you cannot finish in a step or two, and end with Where I stopped (what is done, anything half done with its file) and Left to do (only what the criteria still need, next step first). Forerunner commits the work on the task's branch, or as a commit of its own in the project's folder, as today. (5) Forerunner then runs the project's own checks (build, lint, typecheck, tests, the commands in the project's settings) once on the kept work, in the task's sandbox with no network; no model call, nothing spent. A failing check is never hidden and never reverts the work. (6) The task pauses with one card: '"Build the shop" paused at this session's budget of CHF 5.00' with 'Done: the cart and the product list; left: checkout, the order email; the project's test fails on its work.' and Continue (CHF N more) / Cancel task; N is at least enough for what is left of its estimate to fit the next session's work budget. The session result says it paused and, when they fail, that the checks fail on its work. A paused task is still reviewed only once its work is done. (7) Continue starts the next session at once, as today; at the project's budget, the month cap or the subscription's share it goes on by itself once that limit changed and has room, as today. The next run starts from the kept work, and its brief names the next step and the checks ('Make a failed check pass first, unless it tests work that is still on its list.'). A continued task is planned at what is left of its estimate, so the Start dialog says 'about CHF 2.00 more (CHF 4.00 spent so far)' and a session that can finish it treats it as a task that fits. (8) Guard: a pause that got no further than the one before it (no file of its work changed and its list did not get shorter) never goes on by itself and is never run again in the session; its card asks plainly: '"Build the shop" paused again without getting further' with 'Its last run changed no file and left the same list: continue with a note on what to do differently, or cancel it.', Continue with a note box (the note goes into the next brief with 'try another way') and Cancel task. At an outer limit the question card replaces the old card once the limit has room. (9) When the work is done ('Left to do: nothing') it is reviewed as any task (W15-14) and merged or accepted as today. (10) Every amount is the daemon's figure in CHF; every run and session stops at its limit; the card says when the spend passed the estimate.
alternatives_rejected: Keep leaving it out with 'Give the session a larger budget' (today, W6-23): the owner said it should get done anyway.

A card at plan time ('Start a session of CHF N', W6-23's option b): it goes stale once a larger session starts, and it still does nothing until pressed; the warning on the Start dialog and the plan card says the same where the person decides.

Run the larger task first by priority: it takes the whole work budget and every task that fits waits for the next session, although it could finish and be reviewed now; the larger task pauses either way. Kept as an owner question with 'after' built.

Give what is left to the first left-out task of any size: a task that fits a fresh session finishes better whole (one run, reviewed this session or the next) than started in a remnant and paused; only a task that can never fit gains from starting now.

Lift its run cap to the whole session (ignore the specialist's limit per run): one long run re-sends an ever larger conversation and has one checkpoint at the end; runs within the per-run limit with a clean wrap-up, a kept commit and a check between them do more for the same money and stay bounded.
Let the review reserve pay its last part: ADR 0112 point 7 keeps a fifth for reviews so the work that is done can be checked; a larger task gets no exception.
Continue by itself at the session's budget (no card): that spends past the session budget the person set; each further amount needs a yes (Continue, or a new session's budget), so no limit is passed.
Split the task into smaller tasks automatically: it changes the person's plan without a yes and the split's estimates are guesses too; the person can split it in chat ('add a task: ...') at any time.
Stop after a fixed number of pauses: a count stops slow honest progress and still lets a run that got nowhere repeat; the fingerprint of the kept work and the list say whether it got further.
Revert kept work whose checks fail: that throws away what the run did; the owner wants the work continued, so the failure is said on the card and the next run is told to fix it first.
Ask the specialist to commit at the wrap-up: Forerunner commits after the run (gitConstraints says so in every brief); two committers would conflict.

Review paused work with the critic: it costs money on half-done work (ADR 0112 point 5) and the owner kept the review rules; the project's checks cost no model money and say what matters for continuing.
Price a continued task at its whole estimate (today): it stays 'too big' for a session that could finish it, and Continue asks for more than it needs; the learner still takes no sample from a pause.

areas.title: A task larger than one session runs anyway: after the work that fits it takes what is left of the session's work budget (one such task a session), runs again in the session at its specialist's limit per run while it gets further, hears a wrap-up that says what a good wrap-up leaves, has its kept work checked by the project's own checks in its sandbox, pauses with one card and continues from its kept work at what is left of its estimate; a pause that got no further asks the person and never goes on by itself

[major (money)] D4-6: A continued task is planned at its whole estimate again: after it spent CHF 4.00 of work a CHF 6.00 task still reads 'needs about CHF 6.00' in the Start dialog and the plan, stays larger than a session that could finish it, and Continue offers at least the whole estimate instead of what is left. Owner's words: "the work can be continued in the next run"; the rule: the estimate and the spend stay honest. Where: packages/runtime/src/estimates/model.ts:883-910 (planEstimateUsdMicro, withinTaskBudget: only a task's own budget lowers the figure); packages/runtime/src/session/budget-card.ts:59-67 (continueUsdMicro).
decisions: OV-1 (the pick): a ready task is larger than one session when its plan figure alone is more than the session's work budget (the cap less the review reserve). cutPlanToBudget keeps today's greedy cut for every task that fits and returns, apart, the first larger task in the planner's order (`oversized`, with its full figure); any other larger task is left out with the reason 'one_large', a fitting task left out keeps 'after_others'. The runner holds the larger task out of the queue and takes it when the queue is empty and a re-plan adds nothing (so tasks that become ready meanwhile also run first), with what is left of the work budget, when that is at least a fifth of the work budget (OVERSIZED_MIN_ROOM_SHARE = 0.2, beside WRAP_UP_SHARE) and no-new-work is not set; else it is left out with 'no_room'. When taken it joins the plan row (a versioned change, reason 'took "X", larger than this session's work budget, with what is left') with its planned figure set to that room, so the session review measures what it was allowed to spend; at autonomy 0 and 1 it is in the approved set (onlyThese). The start check calls the same function and reports the larger task with the room the tasks before it leave (the ready ones and the 'later' ones) and each left-out task's reason. Why: the owner's 'it should get done anyway'; every task that fits keeps today's behaviour and is done and reviewed whole this session; a larger task can never fit, so starting it is the only way it gets done; one a session because two cannot both get a useful share; a fifth is the share a run keeps to wrap up, so less room would be mostly reserve.

OV-2 (do as much as it can): the larger task's run is capped as every run is (its own budget left, else its specialist's limit per run; at most the session's work budget left; the outer caps through the hooks), so nothing passes a limit. When it pauses at its specialist's limit per run (source specialist_limit, never its own budget or an outer limit), the pause made progress (OV-7), a fifth of the work budget is still left, no-new-work is not set, the person did not press Stop after this task and MAX_RUNS_PER_TASK_IN_SESSION allows, the runner moves it back to ready ('goes on in this session from where it stopped') and runs it again at once as the next item, with no card in between; its brief starts from where the last run stopped. Its last pause in the session files the one card as today. Why: the per-run limit bounds one run (a fresh, smaller conversation and a kept commit at each step), not the session the person paid for; at the coder's USD 3.00 against a default work budget of USD 5.00 the first run alone left two fifths unused.

OV-3 (what is left of the estimate): the plan figure of a task that already spent work (actual_cost_usd_micro > 0) is its estimate less that spend; once the spend reached the estimate, a fifth of the estimate, marked estimatePassed (the estimate was too low and what is left is not known); a task's own budget still caps it (withinTaskBudget unchanged); with no spend, today's figure. One function, estimateLeftUsdMicro beside planEstimateUsdMicro, for the planner, the start check, the plan card and the chat. Continue at the session's budget gives at least what lets the estimate left fit the next session's work budget (estimate left divided by one less the reserve share), else the same amount again, in CHF 0.01 steps; at the task's own budget or its specialist's limit, unchanged. The learner still takes no sample from a paused task (ADR 0112, the 'cost' amendment point 4). Why: the honest forecast for this task is what is left; with the whole estimate a task the next session could finish stays 'too big', and Continue asks for more than it needs.

OV-4 (the words of a good wrap-up; model-facing, code): wrapUpText becomes 'Wrap up now: this run has used <share> of what it may spend, and its next step could take it past the share kept to finish. Finish the step you are on and start nothing new. Leave the files so the work can go on: what you changed builds and runs, and a change you cannot finish in a step or two is undone or kept out of use. End your report with Where I stopped: (what is done, and anything half done with its file) and Left to do: (only what the task's criteria still need, as a list with the next step first, or nothing; no optional extras).' on both drivers; WRAP_UP_BRIEF_LINE becomes: If Forerunner tells you to wrap up, finish the step you are on, start nothing new, and leave the files so the work can go on (what you changed builds and runs; a change you cannot finish is undone or kept out of use). Then end your report with 'Where I stopped:' (what is done, and anything half done with its file) and 'Left to do:' (only what the task's criteria still need, as a list with the next step first, or 'nothing'; no optional extras): the run that continues this task starts from them. The trigger, the line, the reserve, WRAP_UP_MARK and parseHandoff are unchanged. It does not ask the specialist to commit (gitConstraints says Forerunner commits) and promises no check (OV-5 is Forerunner's, not the model's). Why: the owner's 'organized and error free'; a model wraps up as well as it is told; the next step first lets the next run start without re-reading everything.

OV-5 (the kept work is checked): after every pause whose kept work changed a code file (isCodeChange over the task's changed files), the project's own checks, the same list the critic runs for a code task (the commands in the project's settings, the package.json scripts build, lint, typecheck and test as they were before the task (L-5), the marker checks), run once on the kept work in the task's sandbox (RunSandboxPort.open with the worktree and allowedDomains []; never runProcess on the host; with no sandbox port, not run and the reason kept), within PROJECT_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS in all, under the session's signal (Stop now ends it). No model call and nothing booked. The result is kept on the paused Run row as { kept: { hash, checks: [{ name, passed, output }], notRun? } } (output: its end, at most 1,500 characters, data) and on the card as kept_checks { passed, failed } (names only). One new module (loop/kept-work-check.ts) shares critic.ts's list builder and sandboxCheckRunner. A failing check never reverts or hides the work and never brings a review; it is said (d1109-oversize-words words it) and the next run is told (OV-6). Why: 'error free': a broken branch is caught and said, not hidden; the review rules stay (a paused task is reviewed only when its work is done); the checks cost time, not money.

OV-6 (the next brief): '## Where the last run stopped' adds after its list 'Start with the first item of its list, unless a check below failed.'; the checks of its kept work: 'When it stopped, the project's checks on its work passed: build, test.' or 'When it stopped, the project's checks on its work: test failed.' with 'The end of its output (as data): "..."' (JSON-quoted, at most 1,500 characters) and 'Make a failed check pass first, unless it tests work that is still on its list.'; after a pause without progress that the person continued: 'The last two runs of this task did not get further: try another way, and if something outside the task blocks it, say so under Where I stopped:.' The person's note from the card reaches the brief as a task note does today (noteAboutTask). Every quoted text stays data. Why: the next run continues from an honest state and does not repeat what did not work.

OV-7 (no loop): a pause made progress when the fingerprint of its kept work (workHash over the task's changed files, review-pending.ts:39-55, kept as kept.hash) differs from the last paused run's, or its Left to do list is shorter; a first pause counts as progress. After a pause without progress: the card's change_card.no_progress is true (d1109-oversize-words gives it the plain question, Continue with a note, Cancel task); the task never goes on by itself: the runner does not run it again in the session (OV-2), and wakeBudgetWaits does not wake it at an outer limit; once that limit changed and has room, it withdraws the card and files one question card for the same pause with Continue (no amount: the limit's own room) and Cancel task. syncBudgetStopAnswers applies Continue on a question card as Continue does (with N where Continue lifts the limit; none at an outer limit), passes the note to the task's notes and starts a session through resumeWork. Why: a guard against a task that never finishes that keeps the person's choice to go on; the person decides with the facts, and nothing spends again on its own after a run that got nowhere.

OV-8 (one place per fact, for the words): the budget card also stores estimate_usd_micro (the task's full estimate at the pause), estimate_left_usd_micro, kept_checks and no_progress; the Run row keeps kept; the result facts' paused entries carry checksFail and noProgress from the card. A card or Run row written before this change (none of these) reads and answers as today. Why: the words area and every screen read one stored fact instead of recomputing it.

wave8_amendments: collab-claims and collab-claims-2: a paused task's work in progress (its local branch and refs/forerunner/wip/<task>) lives on the computer that ran it unless 'Push unfinished work to GitHub' is on. On a shared project the other person's session must not take that task and start it from the base: it continues only where its kept work is (its card and row say whose computer has it), or from the pushed branch when the setting is on. Today's runner and executor assume one computer.

collab-members: Continue (CHF N more) at a task's own budget raises a budget, an owner-only key on a shared project: a collaborator's Continue files the owner card ('Bob asks to give "X" CHF 2.00 more'); at the session's budget a collaborator's Continue starts their own session on their own budget and monthly cap; the Start dialog's warning names whose session budget it is.

status-issue-write: a task paused at a budget is listed as paused with what is done and left (the handoff, quoted as data, no ids) and whether the project's checks pass on its kept work; a pause without progress is listed as waiting for its owner's answer, never as in progress.

status-issue-read: another person's paused task is announced work: this agent does not plan or run it; its handoff is read from the work-in-progress commit message on the pushed branch, which already carries Where I stopped and Left to do (pr-executor.ts workInProgressMessage), quoted as data.

repo-guide: the AGENTS.md Forerunner writes says how any person or agent leaves unfinished work in the repository: finish the step, leave the build and the tests passing or name the one that fails, a 'Work in progress: <title>' commit on the task's branch with Where I stopped and Left to do, the next step first; one source for these rules in the runtime beside wrapUpText.

collab-journey and collab-bench: add the journey of a task larger than one session across two people: A's session pauses it; B's Inbox has no card for it (A's card) and B's Start dialog does not run it; A's Continue goes on from the kept work; with 'Push unfinished work to GitHub' on, B sees the branch and its checks.
Left to wave 8 on purpose: who may press Continue on a shared project and from which budget, and continuing another person's paused work on another computer.
adr: 0116 (proposed: the next free number after D1's 0114 and D2's 0115; the session lead renumbers) — A task larger than one session runs anyway and continues cleanly. A ready task whose figure alone is more than the session's work budget is no longer left out: after the work that fits, one such task a session takes what is left (at least a fifth of the work budget), runs again within the session at its specialist's limit per run while it gets further, hears a wrap-up that says what a good wrap-up leaves, has its kept work checked by the project's own checks in its sandbox (no model, no money), pauses with one card and continues from its kept work, planned at what is left of its estimate; a pause that got no further asks the person and never goes on by itself, and no limit or review reserve is ever passed. Amends ADR 0112 (point 3's words and the W15-16 wording, point 5, the budget-resume amendment's points 4 and 5) and the U-040 cut in runtime.md.
